build: Ocean type 1 cartridge, 16 banks of 8 KB (128 KB)

comments.text: The first 11 bytes of Stage 4's data block, loaded from $0C01. Bytes 2-4 are the stage's three background colours ($D021-$D023; stage_setup_tables copies them to bg_colour0-2): 00, 03, 0B here. Byte 5 (0B) is the number of the last section, which track_stage_section and init_round_state read. Bytes 6-7 ($8862) point into cartridge bank 0 to the 64 bytes of stream records that load_stage_bank_records copies to $0100. Bytes 8-9 ($8989) point to the list of animation ids that the helper at $06E6 searches, and byte 10 (39) is that list's last index. Bytes 0 and 1 (78, 21) are read by nothing in play.

The 22 bytes $0C0C-$0C21 are Stage 4's eleven table pointers; stage_setup_tables copies them to $2A-$3F (map_row_lo_ptr, map_row_hi_ptr, block_chars_ptr, block_props_ptr, path_table_ptr, $34, script_ptr_a, script_ptr_b, anim_lo_ptr, anim_hi_ptr and $3E). Their values here are $19D3, $19F4, $0D3A, $1996, $1B40, $1D5C, $1E5B, $1E8D, $1E0E, $1DD4, $1E48.

Colour of each character code in Stage 4, 256 bytes, indexed by the character (screen code) found in the screen buffers. recolour_screen copies the entry for every one of the 840 playfield characters into colour RAM. Only the low nibble reaches colour RAM, and a value of 8 or more turns on multicolour for that character, since the playfield runs in multicolour text mode ($D016 bit 4).

Table of section record addresses for Stage 4: one word for each of its 12 sections, $0D22-$0D39, starting $1A15, $1A2E, $1A47 and on, each 25 bytes on. store_section_index indexes it with section_index times 2, track_stage_section with the next and the previous section's index times 2, and init_round_state with the last section's ($0C06); stage_setup_tables reads the first word through $24.

The map block table of Stage 4: four screen characters for each of 61 block numbers (upper left, upper right, lower left, lower right), $0D3A-$0E2D, pointed to by block_chars_ptr ($2E). The table's length depends on the stage.

The block numbers of Stage 4's map, one byte for each block position, from $0E2E to $1995. map_row_lo/hi_table give each of the 33 rows' start (first $0E15, $0E51, $0E8D); rows differ in length, and a row's pointer is biased by the row's first column, so the byte for block column x is at the row pointer plus x. Each byte indexes block_chars and block_props_table.
Bytes $122E-$162D of map_rows_data ($122E is 1024 bytes in).
Bytes $162E-$1995 of map_rows_data ($162E is 2048 bytes in).

Map block properties of Stage 4, one byte for each block number: 61 bytes $1996-$19D2, matching the 61 four-character blocks of block_chars ($0D3A-$0E2D). block_props_ptr ($30) points here. Bit 0 solid, bit 1 harmful, bits 2 and 3 slopes, bit 5 enter mode 1, as block_property_at and the terrain probes test them. The values present are $00, $01, $04, $05, $08, $09, $40, $43.

Map row address table, low bytes: 33 entries $19D3-$19F3, one for each row of Stage 4's map. map_row_lo_ptr ($2A) points here and stage_setup_tables copies the pointer from $0C0C. The high bytes are the 33 bytes at $19F4.

Map row address table, high bytes: 33 entries $19F4-$1A14. map_row_hi_ptr ($2C) points here and stage_setup_tables copies the pointer from $0C0E. The low bytes are map_row_lo_table at $19D3; a row starts at hi:lo.

The 12 section records of Stage 4, 25 bytes each, $1A15-$1B40: section_table ($0D22) holds their addresses. Each record begins with the follow zone (zone_left, zone_right, zone_top, zone_bottom) and the view limits that update_view_scroll reads through section_ptr ($26), and holds the flags byte at offset $16 (section_scroll_flags); the rest of the 25 bytes is not decoded here. Two fields are rewritten at the start of a round: stage4_patch stores $00C0 in bytes 12-13 of section 7 ($1AD0-$1AD1, the largest view_top) and $0410 in bytes 8-9 of section 8 ($1AE5-$1AE6, the largest view_left); the handler at $A82A (entry 8 of the obj_flags handler table at $A868, not the obj_kind type-8 handler $A981) later writes $0160 into the first pair. Bytes 6-13 of a record are the view limits: smallest and largest view_left, then smallest and largest view_top, a word each.

Table of path data addresses that path_table_ptr ($32) points to, indexed by obj_arc_state; the pointer is one below the first entry in the stage 1 table, so the table's first word may start at $1B41. The pointer at $34 is $1D5C. The area from $1B41 to $1D5B is 539 bytes; the format of its words is as in stage 1's path_address_table.

The table the pointer at $34 (a copy of $0C16, here $1D5C) points to: script command 22 ($B722) reads it through ($34) at $B72D to find the record of an object it sets up. In stage 1 the first path data and these records lie together in this area; where this stage's path data ends is not established.

High bytes of the addresses of Stage 4's animation data blocks, 58 entries $1DD4-$1E0D indexed by animation number; anim_hi_ptr ($3C) points here. The low bytes are the 58 bytes of anim_lo_table at $1E0E.
Low bytes of the addresses of Stage 4's animation data blocks, 58 entries $1E0E-$1E47, indexed by animation number; anim_lo_ptr ($3A) points here. The partner of anim_hi_table.

The eleventh table of Stage 4, which $3E points to (stored by stage_setup_tables from $0C20): the hit reactions 0 and 1 ($A8FA, $A8D8) replace an object's obj_anim_num with the entry at that index, so it maps an animation number to the animation the object switches to when hit. It starts at $1E48.

Low bytes of the addresses of Stage 4's object movement scripts: 50 entries $1E5B-$1E8C, the table that script_ptr_a ($36) points to. object_script_step loads the pair (script_ptr_a, script_ptr_b) into $E3/$E4 and then reads the script byte at ($E3) + obj_script_pos ($379C,x). The high bytes are script_addr_hi.
High bytes of the addresses of Stage 4's object movement scripts: 50 entries $1E8D-$1EBE, the table that script_ptr_b ($38) points to; the low bytes are script_addr_lo.

Object movement script bytes of Stage 4, from $1EBF; the scripts start between $1EBF and $231F. A byte below $80 is a command number: object_script_step looks it up in script_cmd_lo/hi at $B33C/$B35F and runs it; a byte with bit 7 set is a move (low four bits the direction, next byte the repeat count).
Bytes $22BF-$2323 of script_data ($22BF is 1024 bytes in).
Stage 4 entry for table indexes 6, 10, 20, 21 and 25. Sets obj_kind,x to $40 when obj_off_y,x is non-zero, otherwise to the value in $3633 (obj_kind of object 68). Returns immediately.

Stage 4 entry for table index 22. A scripted-movement state machine for one object: sets $14=$42, then uses state bytes at $BF22-$BF25 just past the code end ($BF25 non-zero selects phase 1). Phase 0 waits on timer $BF22, reads the next entry of stage4_move_script_table at index $BF24, and either stores fixed values in object bytes ($3310, $3311, $340D, $368E and others) or starts phase 1 by storing the entry in $BF25 and setting obj_arc_state,x=$80 and obj_arc_counter,x=$24; it then loads the next table byte into $BF22 and returns at $BDED. Phase 1 moves $E7/$E8 by 3 left or right per stage4_move_dir_table, watches obj_arc_state bit 6 with $E9=$CC, counts $BF25 down and ends by clearing obj_arc_state. Only the phase-1 paths finish at $BE42, which writes $E7-$EA plus offsets into $392E, $398B, $39E8 and $3A45 (probably a linked part's position).
Common tail: copies $E7/$E8 (+$14) and $E9/$EA (+$09) into $392E/$398B/$39E8/$3A45.

Data, 30 bytes ($BE67-$BE84): timer/command values read as $BE67,y in stage4_scripted_move_step, where y is the index in $BF24 wrapping at $1E. Zero selects patch variant A, a positive value starts the move phase, bit 7 set selects patch variant B (probably); other bytes are timer values loaded into $BF22.

Data, direction flags read as $BE84,y in stage4_scripted_move_step: zero adds 3 to $E7/$E8, non-zero subtracts 3. Only $BE84-$BE90 are plainly flag data; the indexing can reach further, so the exact length is uncertain.

Stage 4 entry for table index 23. If obj_off_y,x is non-zero it decrements it and returns. Otherwise, when $3EBC,x (obj_anim_index) equals 2, it sets obj_off_y,x=$32, $34E2,x=6 and $3323,x=0, then jumps to resident $4C9D (probably launching or changing the object).

Stage 4 entry for table index 24. Moves the object whose position is in $E7-$EA: adds obj_speed,x to x, then returns if y is $0137 or more; otherwise adds obj_motion_alt,x to y, and on every 8th frame (frame_count & 7 zero) increments obj_motion_alt,x (probably gravity, capped at 4) when the object's x is above player_box_left ($4C/$4D) minus $80, using $48/$49 for that sum. All exits are the rts at $BEFE.

The character set of the playfield for Stage 4, $C000-$C4C7 (1224 bytes loaded by the stage's character set directory entry): eight pixel rows for each character, starting at character $00 (VIC bank 3, $D018 $21 or $31). stage_load copies it from the cartridge at stage start.
Bytes $C400-$C4C7 of stage_charset ($C400 is 1024 bytes in).
